players.product: Enterprise SATA SSDs, PCIe SSDs and RDIMM modules for AI servers and data centers; mSSD and embedded storage

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): its HLC (high-level cache) technology, built on its self-developed controller chips, firmware and system architecture, lets SSD or UFS devices take over warm/cold data caching from DRAM, reducing device DRAM requirements; it is adapting HLC with AMD, UNISOC, a leading global SoC company and a leading global CPU company; joint tuning with AMD on AI mobile workstation and AI PC platforms showed AI PC model scale up about 3.2x and memory utilization efficiency up about 200%.

Management (IR record): its AIDIMM memory reaches up to 128GB capacity and up to 307.2GB/s bandwidth, uses four LPDDR5x packages on one side and fits mainstream agent-host motherboards, targeting AI PCs and agent hosts.

Management (IR record), citing third-party information: AI deployment in the cloud and on devices will bring large incremental storage demand, while overseas original manufacturers keep relatively cautious NAND capex and grow NAND supply moderately through technology upgrades, so storage supply and demand will stay tight.

Management (IR record): controller chips, enterprise storage and mSSD, where it invested early, have made substantive commercial progress, and it keeps raising the revenue share of high-end customers; with storage wafer prices rising, the cost impact is reflected in operating costs under monthly weighted-average inventory costing.

Longsys.why: NAND-based storage maker (own controller chips) shipping enterprise SATA/PCIe SSDs and RDIMMs into AI servers and data centers; sells more as AI storage demand grows.
Longsys.evidence: Longsys investor Q&A: SZSE Interactive Easy (09-18-2026): enterprise storage products are widely used in AI servers and data centers; volume shipments of SATA SSD, PCIe SSD and RDIMM.
